near_duplication.caveat: cross-burst pairs come almost entirely from the single class (E) with >1 burst -- this estimate is not class-balanced and should not be read as precise; it is directionally indicative only, given n_pairs above.

leakage_demo.interpretation: The near-100% naive-split accuracy is an artifact of near-duplicate frames from the same continuous recording burst appearing on both sides of the split. The burst-disjoint collapse is not a measure of poor model quality either -- most classes have only ONE recording burst, so holding a burst out removes that class from training entirely. Neither number estimates real-world generalization; see docs/data_collection_protocol.md.

repeated_split_stats.interpretation: A same-burst 1-NN collision rate this high means the reported accuracy is dominated by near-duplicate matching within a burst, not sign discrimination.
repeated_split_stats.pseudo_replication_caveat: The 20 seeds are overlapping 80/20 resamples of the same 842 rows, not 20 independent datasets -- this measures sensitivity to split randomness, not true sampling variability, and likely understates real-world variance.

insample_comparison_caveat: Trained and evaluated on the SAME data (all of it) -- this measures whether each classifier's capacity suffices to fit the observed classes with this feature representation, not whether it generalizes to unseen signers/sessions. Latency is single-sample CPU inference on the development machine (see environment.processor), not the deployment device, and excludes MediaPipe detection time.
feature_ablation_caveat: In-sample fit only, same caveat as section 4.
